definitions.explanation: Western-influenced dishes as adapted in Japan. Does not typically refer to authentic Western cuisine but rather to a distinctly Japanese style of cooking that originated from Western recipes introduced during the Meiji era. Classic examples include ハンバーグ (hamburger steak), オムライス (omurice), コロッケ (croquettes), and エビフライ (fried shrimp).

notes:
USAGE:
{洋食|ようしょく} refers specifically to the Japanese adaptation of Western dishes, not to Western cuisine as served in its countries of origin. It forms a pair with ⟦{和食|わしょく}→和食：10436_washoku⟧ (Japanese food). Typical {洋食|ようしょく} dishes include ⟦ハンバーグ→ハンバーグ：01785_hanbaagu⟧ (hamburger steak), オムライス (omurice), ⟦カレー→カレー：02898_karee⟧⟦ライス→ライス：08838_raisu⟧ (curry rice), ⟦コロッケ→コロッケ：10857_korokke⟧ (croquettes), and ⟦ナポリタン→ナポリタン：30400_naporitan⟧ (Napolitan spaghetti). A {洋食|ようしょく}{屋|や} is a restaurant specializing in these dishes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {洋食|ようしょく}{屋|や}: Western-style restaurant
- {洋食|ようしょく}⟦メニュー→メニュー：11166_menyuu⟧: Western-style menu
- ⟦{和食|わしょく}→和食：10436_washoku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{洋食|ようしょく}: Japanese and Western food
- {洋食|ようしょく}⟦レストラン→レストラン：01048_resutoran⟧: Western-style restaurant
